primary_claim: In an improved sparse-pixel image debate/consultancy experiment, against a frozen judge consultancy's selection accuracy degrades as agent capability grows (3.1-22.8% drop) while debate stays flat, but debate barely exceeds an ensemble-of-random-masks baseline, suggesting the adversary mainly acts as a regularizer against reward hacking rather than via the intended computational-complexity mechanism; with judges trained on-policy, no debate configuration meaningfully beats consultancy either, indicating debate's advantage in this setup is not a generalizable protocol-level effect

effect.metric: selection accuracy (%) vs. agent capability (quantilizer q) and vs. protocol (debate/consultancy), across 6 image dataset variants
effect.value: consultancy selection accuracy falls monotonically from zero-capability endpoint by 3.1% (raw MNIST) to 22.8% (whitened MNIST); debate stays within -4.0% to +1.8% of that endpoint at full capability; at matched capability debate margin over endpoint ranges +0.40% to +2.87%

contradicts_or_qualifies: extends and qualifies the original 2018 AI Safety via Debate sparse-pixel experiment (which only compared debate to random selection, not consultancy, and used untrained judges): with matched selection budgets and trained judges, debate does not clearly beat consultancy

the theoretical computational-complexity argument for debate (judge with limited compute but otherwise unbiased) predicts debate should beat consultancy once the judge plays its optimal policy; the trained-judge results do not bear this out in this environment
stated_future_work: test whether smarter/bigger judges on more complex images could leverage the debate structure better
test pixels accompanied by text arguments, with an evidence-only ablation control
test a minimal symbol-based argument channel in other task settings
run debate with VLMs trained via SFT/RL as debaters and judges
test debate as an iterated game rather than simultaneous proposal, especially the last-d_B protocol
give asymmetric evidence budgets to A and B (e.g. 3 cells vs 1 cell) for a fairer judge-accuracy comparison
limitations_stated: results are specific to this toy pixel-selection environment and may not generalize to more realistic settings such as text-based judging
a minimal symbol-argument-channel test produced a clean null but it's unclear whether other optimization dynamics could find a use for such a channel
comparing debate against consultancy on judge accuracy may be unfair since debate reveals fewer relevant cells (half chosen adversarially)
the D2 judge design (trained to output P(claim correct) directly) collapsed to chance and was dropped
quote: This suggests that against an untrained judge debate is mostly acting as a regularizer: it stops the agent from reaching the rare masks that 'hack' the classifier, rather than adding anything through the adversarial structure itself. The trained-judge experiments support that reading: there, where the judge is no longer exploitable, no debate configuration meaningfully beat consultancy either.
